paper.title_en: Closure of averaged Einstein equations by DESI data
paper.abstract_en: We benchmark the hypothesis that the redshift dependence of postulated dark energy in the standard model, measured by the DESI collaboration, is a natural outcome of dark energy-free models of structure formation in general relativity. We recall fundamental results and the properties of averaged dust cosmologies that suggest to replace the dark energy equation of state through the nonperturbative impact of the inhomogeneous geometry. The relevant mechanism can be phrased in terms of an effective mean field description of inhomogeneities using the fluid analogy of a scalar field (the `morphon'). Without violating energy conditions this effective field exhibits a cross-over to phantom behaviour, compatible with observations. The exact dark energy-free framework needs a single closure condition that we implement in terms of parametrizations of the 3-years data of the DESI team. The resulting redshift dependence of effective cosmological characteristics is then illustrated and subject to physical interpretation. The aim of this paper is to set a benchmark that has to be met by any structure formation model or simulation investigated within general relativity in a flow-orthogonal foliation of spacetime, given the hypothesis.
